name: Parametric MST
description: You are given $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$. For any real number $$$t$$$, consider the complete weighted graph on $$$n$$$ vertices $$$K_n(t)$$$ with weight of the edge between vertices $$$i$$$ and $$$j$$$ equal to $$$w_{ij}(t) = a_i \cdot a_j + t \cdot (a_i + a_j)$$$. Let $$$f(t)$$$ be the cost of the minimum spanning tree of $$$K_n(t)$$$. Determine whether $$$f(t)$$$ is bounded above and, if so, output the maximum value it attains.
input_specification: The input consists of multiple test cases. The first line contains a single integer $$$T$$$ ($$$1 \leq T \leq 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases. Description of the test cases follows. The first line of each test case contains an integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \leq n \leq 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of vertices of the graph. The second line of each test case contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ ($$$-10^6 \leq a_i \leq 10^6$$$). The sum of $$$n$$$ for all test cases is at most $$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, print a single line with the maximum value of $$$f(t)$$$ (it can be shown that it is an integer), or INF if $$$f(t)$$$ is not bounded above.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1656F — Parametric MST [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
